title: Connect, sign, send
takeaway: Connecting shows your address, signing can give permission, and sending moves money, so stop and read before the last two.

cards.title: Just a login?
cards.body: You open a site and tap Sign in. Your wallet shows a popup. The top line says Sign in to Dragon Hatch, and there is no gas fee. It looks like nothing. But there are more rows below the welcome line. Read every row before you decide.

value.label: Welcome line
value.why: The welcome line itself is normal.

value.label: Spender
value.why: A login never names a spender.

value.label: Unlimited value
value.why: A login never sets an amount.

value.label: Deadline
value.why: A login has no spending deadline.

cards.title: Connect: the door
cards.body: Connecting lets a site see your wallet address and what it holds. It cannot move anything by itself. But it opens the door to the next two steps, so connect only to sites you reached from your checked bookmark. Disconnecting later only hides your address again. It does not cancel any permission you already gave.

cards.title: Sign: words with power
cards.body: Signing costs no gas, but some signatures hand over your tokens. A plain, readable sign in message with no token, amount, spender or deadline cannot move funds. Typed data that names a spender, value or deadline, a marketplace order, or unreadable hex is not a login. Reject it.
points: Spender, value, deadline or order: reject unless you started it.

cards.title: Send: money moves
cards.body: Sending is a transaction. It moves ETH or NFTs, or calls a contract, and costs gas. Once confirmed, it cannot be undone. Read the action, the amount and the site. If anything differs from what you started, like a higher price or an approval you never asked for, press Reject.
points: A hardware wallet confirms whatever you approve. Read its screen.

cards.title: Try it
cards.body: You tapped Mint for one dragon at the 0.029 ETH presale price. Tap every red flag, then tap Done flagging.

value.label: Mint action
value.why: This is the step you started.

value.label: Price
value.why: Far above the 0.029 ETH you expected.

value.label: Extra approval
value.why: You never asked to approve your NFTs.

value.label: Network fee
value.why: A small gas fee is normal for a transaction.

questions.stem: You connect your mint wallet to a new site. What can the site now do on its own?
options: See your address and what it holds
Move small amounts of your tokens
Read your seed phrase from the browser
List your NFTs for sale on its market
questions.why: Connecting only shares your address. Anything that moves assets needs a signature or a transaction that you approve.

questions.stem: A "Sign in" popup shows a spender, an amount and a deadline. What do you do?
options: Reject it, a login never names those
Sign it, there is no gas fee
Sign it, the title says sign in
Sign it, then disconnect after
questions.why: A spender, value and deadline make it a Permit style approval, not a login. Disconnecting afterwards would not cancel it.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

value.label: Welcome text
value.why: Readable welcome words are not the problem.

value.label: Spender
value.why: A login never names a spender.

value.label: Unlimited amount
value.why: A login never sets an amount.

questions.why: The welcome line is only cover. A spender and an amount turn this into a permission to spend your tokens. Reject.

questions.stem: Which of these signature requests cannot move your funds?
options: Readable text, no token, amount, spender or deadline
Typed data naming a spender and a value
A marketplace order to list your NFTs
A long block of hex you cannot read
questions.why: A plain readable message with no token, amount, spender or deadline cannot move funds. Each of the others can hand over assets.

questions.stem: You disconnected a site yesterday. Can it still use the approval you gave it?
options: Yes, disconnecting does not cancel approvals
No, disconnecting cancels all its permissions
Only if you connect again
Only if you sign in again
questions.why: Disconnecting only hides your address from the site. Approvals stay active until you revoke them.

questions.stem: Your wallet asks you to sign a long string of unreadable hex. What do you do?
options: Reject it, you cannot know what it does
Sign it, hex is normal for many logins
Sign it if the site looks official
Sign it, but use your hardware wallet
questions.why: If you cannot read it, you cannot know what it allows. Reject, and use only sites that show readable requests.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

value.label: Mint action
value.why: This is the step you started.

value.label: Unknown receiver
value.why: A mint pays a contract, not an unknown wallet.

value.label: All your ETH
value.why: Far more than one dragon costs.

value.label: Network fee
value.why: A small gas fee is normal.

questions.why: A send cannot be undone. When the receiver or amount does not match what you started, press Reject.

questions.stem: A friend says: "It is only a signature, no gas, so it cannot hurt." What do you reply?
options: Wrong, some signatures give away tokens
Right, no gas means no risk
Right, only sends move funds
Only hardware wallets make it risky
questions.why: Permit signatures cost no gas and still grant a spender your tokens. In 2025, the largest single phishing theft ScamSniffer recorded, $6.5M, came from one Permit signature.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

value.label: Marketplace order
value.why: A verify step should never be a sale order.

value.label: All your dragons
value.why: Every dragon you hold would be listed.

value.label: Zero price
value.why: Your dragons would sell for nothing.

questions.why: Called verify, it is really a sale order for 0 ETH. Signing lets the scammer buy every dragon for nothing.

questions.stem: Mint day: you used your checked bookmark and tapped Mint. What do you check in the popup?
options: Action, amount and site match what you started
Nothing, the bookmark means it is real
Only that the gas fee looks low enough
That the wallet shows no red warning
questions.why: Even on the right site, read the action, the amount and the site before you confirm. A send cannot be undone.
